title: Enterprise region onboarding prioritization playbook
creator: Asha Menon
description: Playbook to intake, triage, and prioritize enterprise requests for new region availability, residency constraints, and failover requirements. Captures decision criteria, scoring rubric, required artifacts, stakeholders, and escalation paths to standardize handling across PM, Sales, Legal, Security, and Infra teams.
background: Over the past 12 months we have received recurring enterprise asks for region expansion and data residency guarantees tied to procurement and regulatory requirements. Requests vary from simple region enablement to dedicated passive failover and customer-managed VPC deployments. Without a standardized triage flow, responses are inconsistent and slow, impacting win rates and implementation costs.
goals: 1) Reduce average initial response time to region/residency requests to 3 business days. 2) Provide a repeatable prioritization outcome that balances revenue, compliance risk, and operational cost. 3) Produce a canonical set of required artifacts so pre-sales and CSMs can collect complete information up-front.
required_artifacts: Customer name and contract value estimate
Traffic profile: qps, avg token length, burst patterns
Desired deployment model: hosted | dedicated | private VPC | on-prem
triage_steps: Step 1: Intake via standardized form linked above
Step 2: PM reviews artifacts within 3 business days and assigns preliminary priority
Step 3: Quick alignment call with Sales/CS/Legal if impact or compliance ambiguity
Step 4: Technical feasibility review by Infra/Runtime team (3-5 business days)
Step 5: Cost estimate and operational runway analysis by Platform Ops
Step 6: Final categorization and publish decision back to customer with next steps
scoring_rubric: Revenue potential (0-30): ARR impact and contract phase
Compliance urgency (0-30): Regulatory/legal blocker vs nice-to-have
Technical complexity (0-20): infra changes, cross-region replication, failover design
Operational cost (0-10): estimated ongoing run cost
Strategic value (0-10): partner, marquee customer, market entry
priority_thresholds: P0: score >= 75 and regulatory block or >$1M ARR over 12 months
P1: score 55-74 and fixed deadline within 90 days or meaningful enterprise ARR
P2: score 35-54 exploratory asks or longer timeline
P3: score <35 low priority, track for roadmap
acceptance_criteria: Intake form submitted with all required artifacts
PM has assigned preliminary score and routed to Infra/Legal within 3 business days
Feasibility note from Infra and estimated implementation effort in story points
Customer receives decision and implementation ETA or rationale for deferral
escalation_paths: Level 1: PM owner —> schedule cross-functional sync within 48 hours
Level 2: Head of Product & Head of Infra for blocked technical constraints
Level 3: GTM execs + Legal for procurement/regulatory deal escalations affecting go/no-go
edge_cases_and_decisions: Air-gapped/on-prem demands: route to Private Offerings; require separate SOW and security review
Soft-data residency (eg. preference) vs hard legal residency: hard legal wins and triggers P0
Failover-only residency: evaluate read-only KV sync and warm standby cost versus SLA needs
Transient region enablement for trial vs production: offer time-limited region enabling with logging and cost pass-through
communication_templates: Initial acknowledgement email template for Sales/CS to send to customer
Decision memo template to summarize feasibility, estimate, and recommended path
Internal Slack triage thread starter with required artifacts checklist
follow_up_tasks: Create templated intake question set in Salesforce for Sales Engineers
Add scoring UI to internal intake dashboard (Console) for PMs
Schedule quarterly review of scored-but-deferred requests to reassess priority
notes_and_recent_updates: 2026-03-08: Pilot intake trial with three AE teams; average intake completeness improved by 40%
2026-03-10: Legal asked to include explicit list of acceptable transfer mechanisms in required artifacts
2026-03-12: Infra provided preliminary feasibility checklist for warm-standby failover patterns
